questions.q: What happened to the name Amazon SageMaker on December 3, 2024, according to the AWS docs?
options: It was renamed Amazon SageMaker AI, with API namespaces unchanged
It was renamed SageMaker Unified Studio
questions.explain: Amazon SageMaker became Amazon SageMaker AI. The rename did not change existing features; API namespaces, CLI commands and managed policy prefixes kept the sagemaker name.

questions.q: Which of the following is part of a SageMaker AI domain, per the documentation?
options: An associated Amazon EFS volume and a list of authorized users
questions.explain: A domain consists of an associated EFS volume, a list of authorized users, and security, application, policy and VPC configurations.

questions.q: Where do the files of a JupyterLab space live?
options: On its own Amazon EBS volume, not shared with other applications
Only in the domain's shared EFS volume
questions.explain: Applications such as JupyterLab and Code Editor each get their own EBS volume. Keep code in Git and data in S3 rather than relying on a notebook disk.

questions.q: Which environment is free and does not need an AWS account?
questions.explain: Studio Lab is a free service based on open-source JupyterLab that does not require an AWS account.

questions.q: With SageMaker Python SDK v2, what name does Session().default_bucket() use when none is specified?
questions.explain: The SDK v2 source documents the form sagemaker-{region}-{AWS account ID}. Because the name contains sagemaker, the AmazonSageMakerFullAccess managed policy covers it.
